title: Tuna Salad with Light Italian Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: Tuna salad with light Italian dressing is a ready‑to‑eat dish made of canned tuna chunks, fresh vegetables (tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper), leafy greens and a light dressing based on olive oil, vinegar and Italian herbs. The meal is high in protein and low in calories, making it suitable for a light lunch or snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tuna is one of the most popular canned fish thanks to its mild flavor and high nutritional value.
A light Italian dressing typically contains olive oil, wine vinegar, lemon juice and a blend of dried herbs such as basil, oregano and marjoram.
Tuna salad is a staple in many diet plans because it combines high protein with low fat content.
Tuna is rich in omega‑3 fatty acids, which support heart health and reduce inflammation.
In Italy, similar salads are served as “insalata di tonno” especially during the summer months.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Tuna provides a complete set of amino acids, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Help lower triglycerides, support cardiovascular function and reduce inflammatory processes.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: Makes the salad suitable for weight‑control diets while providing a satisfying volume.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tuna is rich in vitamin B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Tomatoes, cucumber and bell pepper supply vitamin C and lycopene, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tuna.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned tuna often contains added salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Mercury exposure
items.content: Regular consumption of large amounts of tuna can lead to mercury buildup; moderation is advised.

items.title: Oil in the dressing
items.content: Even a light dressing adds fat, so portion control is recommended for low‑fat diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The salad is ready to eat straight from the package. It can be enjoyed on its own, wrapped in a flatbread or pita, or used as a filling for sandwiches. For extra flavor, add fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or a few olives.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened package refrigerated at 0 °C – +4 °C. Once opened, consume within 2‑3 days. Discard if the smell or taste changes.
